clue.text: Fellow left with long side of bacon

parts.note: to long for something is to itch for it, a yearning

explanation.surface: Some chap who has gone off with a big slab of bacon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective describing the side, but it is the verb meaning to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: A flitch is a whole cured side of a pig, the traditional cut for curing.

clue.text: Popular term meaning "lavishly"

parts.note: something popular is said to be in, fashionable
a style is a name or title by which someone is called, so a term of address

explanation.surface: A lexicographer notes a fashionable expression that means extravagantly.
explanation.definitionFit: To live in grand fashion is to do things with luxury and flair, freely spending.

clue.text: Back head of uncompromising nature

parts.note: the stern is the back end of a ship
a ness is a headland, a promontory, as in Loch Ness's neighbouring place names

explanation.surface: A rear-facing head of someone who never gives way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is the geographical sense, a headland jutting into the sea, as in many British place names ending -ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Being severe and unbending in temperament is exactly a stern disposition.

clue.text: Ferns found in thickets

definitions.meaning: brake is an old name for bracken, a large fern
a brake is also a dense clump of scrub or undergrowth

explanation.surface: A botanist spots ferns growing within dense undergrowth.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are nouns for vegetation: bracken plants, and patches of dense brushwood.

clue.text: Two ways to become self-effacing

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
ST, short for street, is a way or road

explanation.surface: Advice offering a pair of methods for becoming humble.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'ways' are of different kinds: a method, then a road abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unassuming who plays down their own merits is retiring and humble.

clue.text: German husband takes fellow round east German city

parts.note: Mann is the German word for man or husband

indicators.note: round tells us that the word for fellow goes around the letter for east

parts.note: him, a male person, stands for a fellow

explanation.surface: A man from Germany brings another chap to an eastern German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Mannheim is a large industrial city in Baden-Württemberg, on the Rhine.

clue.text: Bridal gift puts many a man in debt

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, so a large number
someone who owes money is an ower

explanation.surface: A wedding present that leaves the groom owing money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' standing for D relies on the Roman numeral convention: D = 500.
explanation.definitionFit: A dower was the portion a bride brought, or a widow's share of property, a marriage settlement.

clue.text: Referred to one hospital department while conscious

parts.note: a patient referred to a specialist is sent there
I is the Roman numeral one
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A patient was referred to a clinic while still awake.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentient being has feelings and awareness, able to perceive.

clue.text: Enduring a life sentence?

definitions.meaning: enduring as an adjective: lasting a long while
a prison stretch for life is a lengthy spell inside, read literally

explanation.surface: Someone serving life in prison faces a lasting stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting a great while, and literally a lengthy prison stint, both read from the same phrase.

clue.text: Arch sovereign comes round immediately

indicators.note: comes round says the word for sovereign surrounds the word for immediately

parts.note: a king is a sovereign ruler
now means at once, immediately

explanation.surface: A monarch arrives straight away at a gateway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arch' is the adjective meaning sly or mischievous, not a curved structure.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch look is a sly, meaningful one, full of hidden understanding.

clue.text: He initially taught us till our recreation

definitions.text: He initially taught us till our recreation

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of each word that follows it

explanation.surface: A pupil recalls who taught the class right up to playtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A private teacher instructs pupils, the role the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Big-head, in state of elation, found in the garden

indicators.note: in places the head of Big inside the word for elation

parts.note: euphoria is a state of intense happiness

indicators.note: head indicates the first letter of the word Big

explanation.surface: A conceited person, overjoyed, is discovered among the flowerbeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big-head' looks like a conceited person, but it means the first letter of 'Big'.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphorbias are spurges, a large plant genus grown in many gardens.

clue.text: Exercise in a vigorous, energetic way

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words vigorous energetic

explanation.surface: Instructions to work out briskly and with plenty of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a right or skill is to employ it, a verb sense.

clue.text: Saintly virtues displayed by the pope

definitions.meaning: the quality of being sacred or sanctified
His ___ is the formal title by which the pontiff is addressed

explanation.surface: The pontiff shows the qualities of a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanctity is saintliness, and the same word is the pontiff's style of address.

clue.text: A place I malign unhesitatingly

indicators.note: er is the sound of hesitation, so without hesitating means the word loses that pair

parts.note: to malign someone is to slander them

explanation.surface: Someone disparages a location without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhesitatingly' removes ER, the written form of a hesitant pause, from SLANDER to leave SLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is a piece of land, a location, surrounded by water.

clue.text: Put some hours by for recreation

definitions.text: Put some hours by for recreation

parts.words: Put some hours by for recreation
parts.note: setting aside, saving, a few hours for leisure describes the free hours one keeps

explanation.surface: Advice to set aside a few hours for leisure.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure hours not taken up by work are the hours one has free.

clue.text: Item fans resolved to exhibit

indicators.note: resolved here means broken down and reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Supporters decided to show off an object.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhibit a quality is to display it plainly, show it.

clue.text: To dig trenches one needs vitality

definitions.meaning: to dig a covered trench towards an enemy position

explanation.surface: Digging trenches demands plenty of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A military siege verb for tunnelling, and a noun for vigour.

clue.text: Bore witness to a tenor put through his paces

parts.note: T is a standard abbreviation for tenor in music
to put someone through their paces is to test them

explanation.surface: A tenor singer was tried out and vouched for in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to certify or vouch for, so to have testified.

clue.text: A small hearing-aid

parts.note: small refers to a shortened word: the abbreviated name of a device that boosts sound

explanation.surface: Someone describes a tiny device for the hard of hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' means shortened: the word is a clipped form of amplifier, something that makes sound easier to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: An amplifier boosts sound, and its clipped form is a short word.

clue.text: Poorest seaman retired with those left

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going backwards, so the sailor's letters turn round

parts.note: AB, able-bodied, is a rating sailor
the rest are the remainder, those left over

explanation.surface: The poorest sailor goes into retirement with the others remaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Barest means most meagre, having the least, in a superlative sense.

clue.text: The old man's in step

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, the old man
the possessive 's supplies its letter S

explanation.surface: A father's footstep is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A pas is a step in ballet, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Attorney-general about to be left high and dry

parts.note: round and about both mean around

explanation.surface: A senior law officer is about to be abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel stranded on the shore is beached, stuck out of water.

clue.text: Adequate description of 100 per cent test score

definitions.text: description of 100 per cent test score
definitions.meaning: a test with every answer correct, read literally as every one marked correct

explanation.surface: A satisfactory way to describe a perfect exam result.
explanation.definitionFit: Okay or satisfactory, and literally every answer marked correct.

clue.text: Admits it's a permit for wrongdoing

parts.note: to let is to permit
a sin is a wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that it gives licence to misbehave.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone is to allow them entry through a door.

clue.text: Fancy hat worn by executioner

definitions.meaning: a top hat, the tall formal silk hat
to top someone is slang for to kill, so one who does it

explanation.surface: An executioner wears an elaborate hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall silk hat, and slang for a killer who executes.

clue.text: Old VIP wants a whole Stilton, maybe

definitions.meaning: a dated slang term for an important person
Stilton is an English blue cheese, made as large round wheels, so read literally

explanation.surface: An elderly dignitary asks for an entire Stilton.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an important boss, and literally a large wheel of dairy produce.

clue.text: Catch a number taking resin

parts.note: to cop is to catch
L is the Roman numeral 50

explanation.surface: A policeman nabs someone who has taken a number of substances.
explanation.definitionFit: Copal is a hard aromatic tree gum used in varnishes.

clue.text: Cavalry unit made to march

definitions.meaning: a small subdivision of a cavalry regiment
to walk or march in a body

explanation.surface: A mounted company is ordered to march.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalry subunit, and a verb meaning to walk along in step.

clue.text: Infirm priest with little energy needs a break

indicators.note: infirm means weak and unsteady, so the letters of priest are rearranged

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for energy, little meaning abbreviated

explanation.surface: A frail clergyman lacking strength needs some rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Infirm' makes RESPIT, an anagram of PRIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short interval of relief, a pause from something.

clue.text: Unusually animated and sparkling

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of animated are arranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: Someone is exceptionally lively and bright.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamante describes fabric decorated with glittering artificial gems.

clue.text: Impassive team-leader of hefty frame

indicators.note: frame says the word for hefty forms a border around the team's leader

parts.note: hefty means sturdy and solid

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of team

explanation.surface: An unemotional captain with a burly build.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolid means unemotional and unexcitable, showing no feeling.
